chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad bin Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

the supplication in the month of Ramadan, during every night you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You write me among the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, whose Hajj is accepted, their evil deeds expiated from them, their sins forgiven, their striving appreciated.'

And that You make, regarding what You judge and measure from the ordained matter, from the wise decree, during the Night of Predestination, from the judgment that is neither returned nor changed, that You prolong my life, and expand my sustenance, and make me among those by whom You help Your religion, and do not replace me with others.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite every night in Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on the 'decree that is not repelled' (al-qada' al-mahdum), linking nightly Ramadan devotion with the specific blessings of Laylat al-Qadr. It uniquely combines personal petitions for longevity and sustenance with a communal role, asking to be among those who attain accepted pilgrimage (Hajj al-Mabrur) and serve as instruments of divine victory for the faith.
